{{Short description|Formula in 2D conformal field theory}}
In physics, the '''Cardy formula''' gives the entropy of a [[two-dimensional conformal field theory]] (CFT). In recent years, this formula has been especially useful in the calculation of the entropy of [[BTZ black hole]]s and in checking the [[AdS/CFT correspondence]] and the [[holographic principle]].

Using results by [[John Cardy|J. L. Cardy]],<ref name=Cardy1986>{{Citation | last=Cardy | first=John | title=Operator content of two-dimensional conformal invariant theory |journal=Nucl. Phys. B |volume=270 |page=186 |year=1986 |doi=10.1016/0550-3213(86)90552-3 |bibcode=1986NuPhB.270..186C }}</ref> the following entropy formula can be derived:
:<math>S=2\pi\sqrt{\tfrac{c}{6}\bigl(L_0-\tfrac{c}{24}\bigr)}.</math>
Here <math>c</math> is the [[central charge]], <math>L_0 = ER</math> is the product of the total energy and radius of the system, and the shift of <math>c/24</math> is related to the [[Casimir effect]]. These data emerge from the [[Virasoro algebra]] of this CFT. The proof of the above formula relies on [[modular invariance]] of a Euclidean CFT on the torus.

The Cardy formula is usually understood as counting the number of states of energy <math>\Delta = L_0 + \bar{L}_0</math> of a CFT quantized on a circle. To be precise, the [[microcanonical ensemble|microcanonical]] entropy (that is to say, the logarithm of the number of states in a shell of width <math>\delta \lesssim 1</math>) is given by
:<math>S_\delta(\Delta) = 2\pi \sqrt{\frac{c\Delta}{3}} + O(\ln \Delta)</math>
in the limit <math>\Delta \to \infty</math>. This formula can be turned into a rigorous bound.<ref name="Mukhametzhanov Zhiboedov 2019 p. ">{{cite journal | last1=Mukhametzhanov | first1=Baur | last2=Zhiboedov | first2=Alexander | title=Modular invariance, tauberian theorems and microcanonical entropy | journal=Journal of High Energy Physics | publisher=Springer Science and Business Media LLC | volume=2019 | issue=10 | year=2019 | issn=1029-8479 | doi=10.1007/jhep10(2019)261 | article-number=261 | doi-access=free | arxiv=1904.06359 | bibcode=2019JHEP...10..261M }}</ref>

In 2000, [[Erik Verlinde|E. Verlinde]] extended this to certain strongly-coupled (n+1)-dimensional CFTs.<ref name=Verlinde2000>{{cite arXiv | last=Verlinde | first=Erik | title=On the Holographic Principle in a Radiation Dominated Universe | year=2000 |eprint= hep-th/0008140 }}</ref> The resulting '''Cardy–Verlinde formula''' was obtained by studying a radiation-dominated universe with the [[Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker metric]]
:<math>ds^2=-dt^2+R^2(t)\Omega^2_n</math>
where R is the radius of a n-dimensional sphere at time t. The radiation is represented by a (n+1)-dimensional CFT. The entropy of that CFT is then given by the formula
:<math>S=\frac{2\pi R}{n}\sqrt{E_c(2E-E_c)},</math>
where E<sub>c</sub> is the Casimir effect, and E the total energy. The above reduced formula gives the maximal entropy
:<math>S\le S_{max}=\frac{2\pi RE}{n},</math>
when E<sub>c</sub>=E, which is the [[Bekenstein bound]]. The Cardy–Verlinde formula was later shown by Kutasov and Larsen<ref name=KutasovLarsen>{{cite journal | last=D. Kutasov and F. Larsen | title=Partition Sums and Entropy Bounds in Weakly Coupled CFT | year=2000 |arxiv= hep-th/0009244 | doi=10.1088/1126-6708/2001/01/001 | volume=2001 | journal=Journal of High Energy Physics | issue=1 | page=001| bibcode=2001JHEP...01..001K }}</ref> to be invalid for weakly interacting CFTs. In fact, since the entropy of higher dimensional (meaning n>1) CFTs is dependent on exactly marginal couplings, it is believed that a Cardy formula for the entropy is not achievable when n>1.
